newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes resumption of Irish talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes resumption of Irish talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday welcomed the resumption of multiparty talks on the future of Northern Ireland and strongly urged the Irish Republican Army to reinstate its ceasefire immediately.

"I am deeply outraged by the end of the IRA ceasefire, which threatens to plunge Northern Ireland into a senseless spiral of violence. As we start a new year, I call on the IRA to restore its ceasefire immediately," Clinton said in a written statement. He said he was convinced that inclusive talks would soon follow a ceasefire.
White House officials have said that Clinton regards achieving a peace agreement in Northern Ireland as a U.S. foreign policy priority during his second term.

"I have always believed that the Belfast talks will have a better chance of success if all the parties, including Sinn Fein, are at the table, but that can only happen if the IRA declares and implements a ceasefire in both words and deeds," Clinton said.
Sinn Fein, led by Gerry Adams, is the political arm of the IRA.

Clinton, who has met Adams on several occasions in a bid to further the Northern Ireland peace process, said he was convinced that "substantive and inclusive talks would soon follow" if the IRA truce was reinstated.
In 1995, three months before the 1994 IRA ceasefire broke down, Clinton became the first U.S. president to visit Northern Ireland.
